parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing universal exposure is documented: no criminalisation of gender expression, no facility or border restrictions, self-determination gender recognition, hate-speech/discrimination bans, and a travel guide describing a welcoming climate. Positives are documented and institutional, not merely silent. The negatives are real but bounded: equality bodies report rising violence with trans people especially affected, a documented dating-app ambush pattern (physical assault, under-reported), 2019 harassment prevalence at 90% (verbal/psychological, dated), and no statutory hate-crime definition or recording code, weakening prosecution. No trans-specific homicide count, no organised targeting, no state hostility, no custody or ward placement exposure documented. Case counts from equality bodies reflect complaints brought, not rates. The subnational medical-certificate conflict is resident-facing. Net: reduced but nontrivial risk — roughly the 0.65 tier, with the violence pattern and enforcement gap holding it below 0.70.
